observations.content: Overfitting occurs when a model memorizes training noise and performs poorly on unseen examples [1].

Based on the provided documents, overfitting can be prevented or reduced using the following techniques:

1. Cross-validation (which estimates generalization using held-out folds) [2]
2. Regularization (which reduces overfitting by penalizing large weights, such as L2 regularization which adds a squared-weight penalty to the training loss) [3]
3. Early stopping (which ends training when validation loss rises) [3]

Based on chapter 5, the techniques explained are **Regularization** (which reduces overfitting by penalizing large weights, such as L2 regularization adding a squared-weight penalty to the training loss) and **Early stopping** (which ends training when validation loss rises) [1].
